caption:
Same $90K salary, $3,200 less income tax. Here's how it works.

Alex salary-sacrifices $10,000 into super, so taxable income drops to $80,000. In 2026–27 that's $3,200 less income tax and Medicare. The fund takes 15% ($1,500), leaving Alex about $1,700 ahead overall.

The catch: it's locked in super until retirement, the 2026–27 concessional cap is $32,500 (your employer's 12% counts), and lower incomes gain less.

Save this for your pay review.

General info only, not personal advice.
